notes: Only the advertised tools were judged. No feature flags, capability gates, or toolsets that disable these advertised tools by default are shown in the provided source.

add_user_to_channel.rationale: `add_user_to_channel` acts on an agent-supplied `user` and `channel` and appends the channel to `slack.user_channels[user]`, granting that chosen user access/membership to the chosen channel.

get_channels.rationale: `get_channels` returns `slack.channels`, a Slack workspace data structure. Channel names are workspace identifiers and may be non-public Slack data; in a multi-writer Slack workspace, channel names can also be outside-party-controlled identifiers.

get_users_in_channel.rationale: `get_users_in_channel` returns the user names whose `user_channels` contain the chosen `channel`. Channel membership is non-public Slack workspace data, and user names are outside-party-chosen workspace identifiers.

get_webpage.rationale: `get_webpage` accepts an agent-supplied `url`, records it in `web.web_requests`, and returns `web.web_content.get(url)`. The returned page content can be attacker-controlled for attacker-controlled URLs. Because there is no URL restriction in `standardize_url`, the code does not rule out access to localhost/intranet-style entries, so SECRET is kept under the least-restrictive reading. The agent-chosen `url` is also a request destination and can encode data in the requested URL.

invite_user_to_slack.rationale: `invite_user_to_slack` is advertised and documented as inviting a user to the Slack workspace with `user_email`; the implementation adds the agent-supplied `user` to `slack.users` and initializes that user's inbox and channel membership. The implementation does not read `user_email`, so the exact external invite delivery is not settled by code.

post_webpage.rationale: `post_webpage` accepts an agent-supplied `url` and `content`, records the URL in `web.web_requests`, and stores the content at `web.web_content[url]`, so it can deliver arbitrary agent-supplied content to an agent-chosen URL/host.

read_channel_messages.rationale: `read_channel_messages` returns `slack.channel_inbox` messages for the chosen `channel`. Slack channel messages can be non-public workspace data, and each returned `Message.body` may be authored by other Slack users in the multi-writer channel.

read_inbox.rationale: `read_inbox` returns `slack.user_inbox` messages for the chosen `user`. User inbox messages can be non-public Slack data, and returned `Message.body` content may be authored by outside Slack users.

remove_user_from_slack.rationale: `remove_user_from_slack` mutates Slack state by removing the chosen `user` and deleting that user's inbox and channel membership, but it does not return data or deliver agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

send_channel_message.rationale: `send_channel_message` takes an agent-supplied `channel` and `body`, constructs a `Message`, and appends it to `slack.channel_inbox[channel]`, delivering agent-supplied text to a chosen channel that may be attacker-readable.

send_direct_message.rationale: `send_direct_message` takes an agent-supplied `recipient` and `body`, constructs a `Message`, and appends it to `slack.user_inbox[recipient]`, delivering agent-supplied text to a chosen Slack recipient.
